subject.title: Validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox core interpret artifact contents with a built-in schema language, or should schema validation remain part of the repository command that produces the evidence?
rationale: Current documentation intentionally keeps Crabbox generic and assigns proof-schema validation to repository-owned commands, while this proposal introduces a new CLI contract and a partially implemented schema dialect.

options.title: Keep validation repo-owned
options.body: Preserve the existing boundary and document examples using repository-native schema validators before `--require-artifact` checks the resulting proof file.

options.title: Adopt standards-compliant validation
options.body: Approve a built-in gate only with explicit JSON Schema dialect/support semantics, bounded artifact reads, and focused provider capability tests.

options.title: Adopt the proposed subset
options.body: Accept the dependency-free subset and own its documented divergence from full JSON Schema, including how unsupported keywords are surfaced.

recommendation.title: Keep validation repo-owned
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing boundary and document examples using repository-native schema validators before `--require-artifact` checks the resulting proof file.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans the core CLI and provider contracts that define whether this becomes a durable cross-provider command surface.
